video_title: LEBRON AND CAVS REAL SMOKE + CAVS OFFSEASON PLANS - 5 Good Minutes With Windy

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye's comments on the Cavaliers' internal team issues
quotes.excerpt: LeBron doesn't fix the guys not liking each other.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Oldach
text_blocks.text: A comment getting some run here in Cleveland was made by former Cav Channing Frye on the Road Trippin' podcast. The group was talking about where LeBron James is going to play next season, and Channing Frye said that the Cavs have soul issues. He said, quote, 'They got I don't like you issues and I don't want to be here with you issues,' and he said LeBron doesn't fix the guys not liking each other. What in the world is he talking about?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I'm not aware of what he's talking about. I would say that when you watch the Knicks and the Cavs play in the conference finals, you definitely saw one team that showed way more drive and vision and energy and togetherness, but I didn't get the impression that it was because they didn't like each other. I got the impression they were outplayed, and the mental toughness aspect of the conference finals was definitely a factor. Questioning the Cavs' mental and physical toughness is fair to question, but I didn't get any togetherness issues.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' lack of communication with LeBron James during free agency
quotes.excerpt: It's unusual because as you can tell out there, the teams with their free agents are doing their business.
quotes.quote: It's unusual because as you can tell out there, the teams with their free agents are doing their business. Not only getting guys resigned, but getting a good feel for where they are. The Lakers have two choices here. They have $50 million in cap space. They have to use that cap space to sign LeBron on some level if they're going to keep him. And so they either can prioritize LeBron or make him last. The way you prioritize him is by going to him first and getting his contract done first and then using the space you have left over. That's what you would normally do with a star player. Or they can go try to do their other business first and then try to offer LeBron what they have left. It appears like they're looking at option B, because specifically what they're doing right now is they're trying to trade for players into their salary cap space, trying to acquire a player with that $50 million in space and absorb them in. That's allowed in the NBA, and that seems to me right now to be their priority. And so they're prioritizing LeBron second.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Status of the Cavaliers' contract negotiations with James Harden
quotes.excerpt: That deal's been in place since February.
quotes.quote: That deal's been in place since February. The first number will be a three. It'll be in the 30-ish million range, and that will take his number down from I think 43 and will help the Cavs manage their apron issues.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' potential interest in trading for Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: They could get involved in a three-way trade.
quotes.quote: They could get involved in a three-way trade. First off, you don't make a trade, the Kyrie Irving deal notwithstanding, you don't make a trade with a team that you're competing to win the division with. For example, I think Isaiah Stewart would have been a really nice addition to the Cavs as a third big man, especially if you're not certain whether you're going to be able to retain Dean Wade. The Pistons are not sending a player to the Cavs. It's just not happening. Now you could call the Grizzlies up and try to get him that way, but that's just not happening. It's very unlikely that the Celtics and Cavs would do a deal together and send a player that directly could do that.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Possibility of a Jaylen Brown sign-and-trade with the Celtics
quotes.excerpt: You're going to have to explain to me how that trade would make sense if it's for Evan Mobley.
quotes.quote: We're already seeing reports that a Jaylen Brown sign-and-trade with Boston could possibly be in the ether. You're going to have to explain to me how that trade would make sense if it's for Evan Mobley. I don't understand Jaylen Brown, Donovan Mitchell, and James Harden together. I don't see it. And beyond that, even if you got all of them to link arms and sing Kumbaya, you need size. Size is so important in the league today. I'm watching the draft and I'm watching Oklahoma City and San Antonio, two giant teams that got to the conference finals in the West, making moves to add size. Unless you're trading for an MVP-level player, I just cannot endorse trading front-line big men for non-bigs. I just don't think it's a prudent way to go forward, especially if you don't have another option.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' roster management and the future of Max Strus
quotes.excerpt: I would keep an eye on Max Strus.
quotes.quote: I would keep an eye on Max Strus. Dean Wade is going to be expensive, I think more expensive than the Cavs were hoping. I think Keon Ellis could be gone unless they lose Dean Wade. If they lose Dean Wade, I think they re-engineer the concept of Keon Ellis. Max Strus's extension eligible has one year at $19 million left on his contract. I want to see if the Cavs are extending Max Strus or if they have to trade Max Strus. And the reason you would trade Max Strus is so that you could potentially afford to keep Dean Wade.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell's contract extension and the impact on Evan Mobley
quotes.excerpt: You can't trade Evan Mobley if Donovan Mitchell isn't locked in.
quotes.quote: You can't trade Evan Mobley if Donovan Mitchell isn't locked in. If you're trading Evan Mobley for a superstar player that can be your franchise player, okay. If you had done Evan Mobley for Giannis, then that's a different conversation. You can't do it. You just can't, because if something happens with Donovan, I mean you have to operate in the world where Donovan is not assured to be on your roster. I don't think that's what he's saying, but I can't operate differently. So if if Donovan is not going to extend, you can't trade Evan. Because if Donovan leaves one way or another, you're going to have to then make Evan your franchise player.
